# Touch: the controller has not answered

How sure we are: <span class="tag tag-hyp">HYPOTHESIS</span>

## What we know

The reset and chip-select lines read as outputs driven low. The supply and clock enables were written and restored.
With the supply on, the released reset line reads high; with no supply it reads low. The SPI block's idle registers were
read and its clock was already on. A transfer test with no peripheral, using the kernel driver's recipe, moved no counter.

## What we guess

The SPI clock and data pads may be dedicated pins that need no configuration. The controller may need firmware loaded
before it answers. A high reset line could come from a board pull-up or from the controller itself.

## What would settle it

Establish the SPI controller's transfer recipe with no peripheral (a second test, with OpeniBoot's recipe, is built and
not run), then a first check packet, to which a first reply byte of `0xD0` would mean the controller is in its loader.

*This describes an experiment, not a procedure to follow: a step that writes to the phone's hardware is only run after a written description and an explicit decision.*
